cls: Antiretroviral - nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI), thymidine analogue
quick: HIV (>=60 kg): 40 mg twice daily; (<60 kg): 30 mg twice daily - in combination ART
Avoid - do NOT combine with didanosine (fatal lactic acidosis reported in pregnancy)
Contraindicated in HIV (breastfeeding not recommended; drug also excreted in milk)
Reduce dose by CrCl; (>=60 kg) CrCl 26-50: 20 mg q12h; <=25: 20 mg q24h
Use with caution - hepatotoxicity/steatosis risk; discontinue if hepatomegaly/lactic acidosis
Avoid - additive risk of pancreatitis and hepatic toxicity
Lactate/bicarbonate if symptoms, LFTs, signs of neuropathy and pancreatitis, amylase/lipase
summary: Stavudine (d4T) is a thymidine-analogue nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used in combination antiretroviral therapy for HIV-1. It carries a BOXED WARNING for lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis (sometimes fatal, especially with didanosine in pregnancy) and for fatal/non-fatal pancreatitis when combined with didanosine. Major dose-limiting toxicities are peripheral neuropathy and lipoatrophy. Because of mitochondrial toxicity, WHO and guidelines now recommend it be phased out in favor of safer NRTIs.
indications: Treatment of HIV-1 infection in combination with other antiretroviral agents

dosage.n: WHO later recommended 30 mg regardless of weight to limit toxicity

dosage.c: Renal impairment (>=60 kg, CrCl 10-25 or dialysis)
dosage.n: Dose after dialysis on dialysis days

admin: May be taken with or without food
Oral solution: shake well, measure with a calibrated device; keep refrigerated
Always use as part of a combination antiretroviral regimen - never as monotherapy
Do NOT co-administer with didanosine or zidovudine
Adjust dose for body weight and renal function
moa: A thymidine nucleoside analogue that is phosphorylated intracellularly to its active triphosphate (stavudine triphosphate), which competitively inhibits HIV-1 reverse transcriptase by competing with the natural substrate thymidine triphosphate and, once incorporated, causes DNA chain termination. It also inhibits host mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma, accounting for its mitochondrial toxicities.

absolute: Concurrent use with didanosine (fatal lactic acidosis/pancreatitis) - especially in pregnancy
relative: History of pancreatitis or risk factors for it
Hepatic impairment or risk factors for hepatic steatosis (obesity, prolonged NRTI exposure, female)
monitor: Symptoms of lactic acidosis (nausea, fatigue, dyspnea, abdominal pain)

preg: Avoid where possible. The combination of stavudine plus didanosine has caused fatal lactic acidosis in pregnant women and should NOT be used. If stavudine must be used, monitor closely. Safer NRTIs are preferred in pregnancy.
lact: Stavudine is excreted in breast milk. Regardless, HIV-positive mothers should not breastfeed because of the risk of postnatal HIV transmission (in resource-rich settings); contraindicated for that reason.
renal: Stavudine is renally cleared - dose reduction is required in renal impairment. For >=60 kg: CrCl 26-50 mL/min give 20 mg every 12 h; CrCl 10-25 mL/min or dialysis give 20 mg every 24 h (lower doses for <60 kg). On hemodialysis days, give the dose after dialysis.
hepatic: Use with caution; hepatotoxicity and hepatic steatosis can occur. Discontinue immediately if there is rapid rise in transaminases, progressive hepatomegaly, or unexplained lactic acidosis.

major: Didanosine (markedly increased lactic acidosis, pancreatitis, and neuropathy - avoid)
Zidovudine (in vitro antagonism - both are thymidine analogues; do not combine)
moderate: Doxorubicin and ribavirin (may inhibit stavudine phosphorylation - reduced activity)
Hydroxyurea (increased risk of lactic acidosis, pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity, neuropathy)
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - additive risk of pancreatitis and hepatic injury
interactions.diagnostics: May raise lactate, amylase, lipase, and transaminases

common: Peripheral neuropathy (numbness, tingling, burning of feet/hands)
Lipoatrophy (fat loss in face/limbs) with long-term use
serious: Lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis (boxed warning, may be fatal)
emergency: Rapidly ascending motor weakness with respiratory failure

monitoring: Serum lactate and bicarbonate if symptoms suggest lactic acidosis
Liver function tests and clinical assessment for hepatomegaly/steatosis
Amylase/lipase and symptoms of pancreatitis (especially with didanosine)
HIV viral load and CD4 count; renal function for dosing
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed as part of your full HIV regimen - missing doses promotes resistance
Report numbness, tingling, or burning pain in hands or feet promptly - this may need the drug to be stopped
Seek urgent care for unusual tiredness, fast breathing, muscle aches, severe abdominal pain, or vomiting (signs of lactic acidosis or pancreatitis)
Avoid alcohol; report any change in body fat distribution
This medicine controls but does not cure HIV; continue safe practices to prevent transmission
pk: Absorbed rapidly; intracellular activation needed for antiviral effect
Plasma peak within ~1 hour of an oral dose
Plasma half-life ~1-1.6 hours; intracellular active triphosphate ~3.5 hours
Capsules at 25 C (controlled room temperature); reconstituted oral solution refrigerated (2-8 C), discard after 30 days
pearls: BOXED WARNING: lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis (potentially fatal); fatal lactic acidosis with stavudine + didanosine in pregnant women
BOXED WARNING: fatal and non-fatal pancreatitis when combined with didanosine
Dose-limiting mitochondrial toxicities (peripheral neuropathy, lipoatrophy) led WHO and guidelines to phase it out in favor of tenofovir/abacavir
Do not combine with zidovudine (antagonism) or didanosine (additive toxicity)
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it - never take two doses at once. Consistent adherence is essential to prevent HIV resistance.
overdose: Experience is limited; adults given up to 12 times the recommended dose showed no acute toxicity but chronic excess increases risk of peripheral neuropathy and lactic acidosis. There is no antidote; management is supportive. Stavudine is removed by hemodialysis (clearance ~120 mL/min).
